row.evidence: SendGrid's SSO docs say SSO is for Pro, Premier and Marketing Campaigns Advanced, with users added manually, via the SSO Teammates API, or created just-in-time as read-only teammates on first IdP-initiated sign-in; no SendGrid SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: Status changed from gated (June) to none. June's 'SCIM via Twilio Organizations API, private beta, Premier' has no first-party SendGrid source: Twilio's SCIM API is documented for Twilio organization-managed (Console) users and never mentions SendGrid teammates, and SendGrid's SSO and Teammates docs describe only manual SSO teammates, the Teammates/SSO Teammates REST APIs and JIT (read-only Restricted Access, IdP-initiated only). The Okta OIN app is SAML/SWA with JIT only. Prices changed: Essentials now starts at $19.95/mo (June: $14.95-29.95), Pro at $89.95/mo, Premier custom; priced by email volume, not per user, and billed monthly. SSO starts at Pro (also Marketing Campaigns Advanced). JIT-only automation; may be reclassified at merge.

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Up to 1,000 teammates, subuser management, SSO.

scim.notes: Not offered by absence for SendGrid teammates. Twilio's separate SCIM 2.0 API covers Twilio organization-managed Console users only (c28).

auth.notes: Bearer API key; EU regional subusers use https://api.eu.sendgrid.com.

capabilities.notes: create_user = Create SSO Teammate (Pro and above, since SSO is Pro+). Roles are scopes / is_admin.

limitations.text: Free and Essentials allow only one teammate; Pro+ up to 1,000.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML and SWA only; 'supports Single Sign-On and JIT user provisioning'.

entra.notes: SendGrid's guide cites an official SAML integration in the Azure AD Gallery; Microsoft Learn tutorial URL returned 404; no provisioning tutorial found.

open_questions: Whether Twilio Organizations SCIM can manage SendGrid teammates is not documented; June's 'private beta' claim could not be confirmed.
Removing a teammate is a delete; there is no documented deactivate state or session revocation.
No audit-log API or teammate-event webhook documented.
Teammates API rate limits not checked.
Google, OneLogin and JumpCloud catalogue entries not checked.
Whether the Teammates API is usable on the Free Trial is inferred from the one-teammate allowance, not stated.
